title: Holidays
subtitle: campsite, package holiday, breathtaking, picturesque
summary: Describe where you stay on holiday and use the strong adjectives that holiday brochures and postcards love.

lesson.heading: Places to stay
rows: a place where you can pitch a tent or park a caravan
a flat which you rent, where you cook for yourself
accommodation like a hotel but cheaper and with fewer services
cheap accommodation, mainly for young people, often with ten or more people sleeping in bunk beds in one room

lesson.heading: Types of holiday
lesson.text: On a **package holiday** you pay for travel, accommodation and food (sometimes even excursions) in advance. A **cruise** is a holiday spent touring on a boat and stopping off to go sightseeing at different ports. An **adventure holiday** involves unusual, exciting and possibly dangerous activities, and suits **adventurous** people.

examples.text: It's often cheaper to go on a **package holiday**, where everything is paid for in advance.
I'd love to hire a boat and spend a month **cruising** round the Mediterranean.
As soon as we got to the campsite we **pitched** our tent.
At the youth hostel Anya insisted on sleeping in the top **bunk**.

lesson.heading: Writing home from a campsite
lesson.text: Sami is camping in the mountains. It is good to **get away** (go somewhere different for a break); the campsite is **remote** (far from other places) and the road is **winding** (full of bends, not at all straight). The **surrounding** countryside made the **terrifying** drive worthwhile.

examples.text: It's very **remote** and we had to drive up an unbelievably **winding** road to get here.
The views over the **surrounding** countryside made the **terrifying** drive worthwhile.
A narrow **winding** road led up the mountain to the cottage we'd rented.

lesson.heading: Writing home from a city
lesson.text: Francesca is enjoying a city break. A **memorable** holiday is one you will always remember (a strong collocation). Something **fascinating** is extremely interesting; an **impressive** building is grand and makes an impact; a **delightful** hotel is charming; an **inconvenient** one is hard to get to; **exceptional** food is unusually good.

examples.text: This is probably the most **memorable** holiday I've ever had.
The town is absolutely **fascinating**, with lots of very **impressive** buildings.
Our hotel is **delightful** - if a little **inconvenient** from the transport point of view.
The food in this area is **exceptional**.

lesson.heading: Brochure adjectives and what they go with
rows: so magnificent it takes your breath away (= stunning)
only the most special people can use it
makes you feel excited and full of energy
unusual and more exciting than everyday reality
very pretty, as pretty as a picture
still in a beautiful and natural state
so special it does not exist anywhere else

lesson.text: Holiday brochures exaggerate: *breathtaking*, *exclusive* and *unique* all promise far more than *nice* or *good*, so save them for things that really deserve them.

exercises.prompt: Match each place to stay with its description.

pairs.right: somewhere to pitch a tent or park a caravan
a rented flat where you cook for yourself
like a hotel but cheaper, with fewer services
cheap rooms with bunk beds, mainly for young people
a holiday touring on a boat, stopping at ports
travel, accommodation and food paid for in advance

exercises.prompt: At the youth hostel Anya insisted on sleeping in the top ___.
exercises.hint: (one word - youth hostels have these beds)
exercises.explanation: Bunk beds are two beds, one above the other; you sleep in the top bunk or the bottom bunk.

exercises.prompt: As soon as we got to the campsite we ___ our tent.
exercises.hint: (past tense of the verb that goes with tent)
exercises.explanation: You pitch a tent at a campsite.

exercises.prompt: Visitors to our hotel have ___ access to our own private beach.
exercises.hint: (adjective - only special guests can use it)
exercises.explanation: Exclusive access means only the most special people can use the facilities.

exercises.prompt: It's often cheaper to go on a ___ holiday, where everything is paid for in advance.
exercises.explanation: On a package holiday travel, accommodation and food are paid for in advance.

exercises.prompt: Our trip to South Africa was undoubtedly the most ___ holiday I've ever had.
exercises.explanation: A memorable holiday is one you will always remember - a strong collocation.

exercises.prompt: A narrow ___ road led up the mountain to the cottage we'd rented.
exercises.explanation: A winding road has lots of bends and is not at all straight.

exercises.prompt: Which adjective describes a village with very pretty buildings and lots of flowers?
exercises.explanation: Picturesque = very pretty, as pretty as a picture.

exercises.prompt: Which adjective describes a view from the top of a mountain over a magnificent landscape?
exercises.explanation: Breathtaking (like stunning) means so magnificent that it takes your breath away.

exercises.prompt: Which adjective describes a hotel with very expensive facilities and very attentive staff?
exercises.explanation: Luxurious means it provides great comfort.

exercises.prompt: It was a once-in-a-lifetime chance: a truly ___ opportunity.
exercises.hint: (adjective - so special it exists nowhere else)
exercises.explanation: Unique = so special it does not exist anywhere else.

exercises.statement: I wouldn't recommend that hotel. It's extremely remote; it's seven miles to the nearest beach and ten miles to the town.
exercises.explanation: Correct. Remote means far from other places, so everything is a long way away.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order to describe an energetic walk.
exercises.answer: We went for an exhilarating walk along a windswept beach.
exercises.explanation: Exhilarating means it makes you feel excited and full of energy.

exercises.prompt: Is each word the adjective or the noun?
